title: Graph Diffusion History Reconstruction via Feasibility-Aware Markov Chain Monte Carlo Estimation

problem.claim: Reconstructing unobserved diffusion histories on graphs from sparse snapshots is difficult.

gap.claim: Existing approaches face explosive search spaces, complex combinatorial constraints, and scarce training data.

contributions.claim: HERMES uses a two-stage pipeline that estimates diffusion parameters and reconstructs diffusion histories.
It estimates diffusion parameters with a tractable mean-field approximation and estimates expected hitting times using Metropolis–Hastings Markov chain Monte Carlo.
It uses dynamic reachability to enforce compatibility with observed snapshots and parameterizes the proposal distribution with a graph neural network trained to match the posterior distribution.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present HERMES as a new method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that HERMES consistently achieves superior performance to existing methods across 12 synthetic and real-world datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph diffusion models propagation across interacting entities in domains including online platforms, infrastructure, social networks, and financial or supply-chain systems.
Diffusion histories are often only partially observed, with a small number of available snapshots and substantial reconstruction difficulty.
HERMES introduces a two-stage process that first estimates unknown diffusion parameters using a mean-field approximation.
The method reduces reconstruction to expected hitting-time estimation and uses constrained Metropolis–Hastings MCMC with dynamic reachability and a GNN-based proposal.
Experiments are reported to show consistent improvement over existing methods across 12 synthetic and real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: The proposal distribution is designed to maintain compatibility with all observed snapshots through dynamic reachability.

interpretation.claim: Encoding feasibility constraints directly into sampling proposals may reduce invalid or inefficient exploration in combinatorial reconstruction problems.

application.claim: Use feasibility-aware proposal mechanisms when reconstructing partially observed discrete histories under hard consistency constraints.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how performance changes when the observed snapshots are sparse, noisy, or inconsistent.

source_observation.claim: The method combines a tractable approximation for parameter estimation with MCMC-based history reconstruction.

interpretation.claim: Separating difficult parameter estimation from structured history sampling can make an otherwise intractable reconstruction problem computationally manageable.

application.claim: Consider staged inference pipelines when exact joint estimation is intractable but approximate estimation and constrained sampling are available.

exception.claim: The abstract does not quantify approximation error or identify conditions under which the staged decomposition is reliable.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the 12 datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or numerical performance differences.
The abstract does not specify the diffusion model, graph sizes, training procedure, or computational cost.
The theoretical proofs referenced in the extended document are not supplied as abstract evidence.
